# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Assistant — verify documented staff effect (staff-assistant)

## Goal
Confirm that `staff-assistant` (Assistant, management-company) is properly defined — card data, parsed typed field, description text and docs — and that it behaves exactly as documented, by adding or tightening a behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope. This card is one of 26 per-card verification children under the parent audit epic `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND`.

## Documented effect (authoritative: GDD Appendix D.4)

- **Ability:** +2 hand slots
- **Scope:** player hand capacity (street-wide)
- **Backing data:** handSlotsAdded=2
- **Engine consumer:** maxHandSize (WeekStart / AiStrategy)
- **Existing behavioural test file:** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Definition verified.** `staff-assistant` in `src/card-data.csv` carries the documented backing data (handSlotsAdded=2), the `description` text states the same effect at the same magnitude using the ×100 consistency rule, and `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` agree.
2. **Parsed field verified.** The typed `StaffCard` field(s) resolve to the documented value (via `parseStaffEffect` for the `effect` column, or the dedicated column) — asserted in a test.
3. **Behavioural test added or tightened.** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` (or a new focused test file) contains at least one behavioural test that asserts the documented effect AND its scope (player hand capacity (street-wide)) — not merely that the card can be hired. The test fails if the effect is absent, mis-valued or leaks outside its documented scope.
4. **Card-level verifier covers it.** `verifyStaffCard` (`tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts`) asserts the same data field, so `unitTestStatus` for `staff-assistant` cannot report `pass` vacuously.
5. **Docs updated.** Code comments and the relevant docs reflect any change made while closing this card; no documentation drift remains for this card.
6. **All tests pass.**

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-assistant` row.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard` typed fields.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — `parseStaffEffect` / template rebuild.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — effect consumer wiring.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` — behavioural test to extend.
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts` — `verifyStaffCard`.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — card catalog row.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — GDD Appendix D.4 authoritative design.

## Impact

Players who hire the Assistant can rely on its printed ability (+2 hand slots, scope: player) actually happening.

# Staff go to business or management company

## Problem statement

Hiring a **business staff** card (e.g. the Delivery Driver, `staff-delivery`) from the general market row does not set `employedAtSlot`, so the two-type model's runtime test (`isBusinessStaffCard` = "has an `employedAtSlot`") classifies the member as **management-company staff**. The member then appears in the management-company roster and Staff Pile, its business-scope effect is inert, its salary is still charged, and there is no way to correct it — the roster offers only *Lay off*, never *Assign to a business*. The player reported exactly this: a hired Delivery Driver "went to the management company" even though its card type is *Business*, and clicking it offered no way to assign it to an appropriate business.

**Chosen model (producer decisions Q1/Q2/Q3).** Business-staff cards are hired **unassigned** into the player's staff pool (the Staff Pile) — there is **no** hire-time destination step; the member receives no business-scope benefits until it is employed, while its salary costs remain. The player assigns an unassigned business-staff member to a business afterwards by clicking it / its roster row (*Assign to business*). The docs that currently promise hire-time placement are updated to describe this assign-later model. Roster and Staff-Pile classification is corrected so unassigned business staff are never shown as management-company staff, and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff so balance runs stop silently wasting hires.

## Users

- **Human player (single-player)** — hires a business-staff card from the market row; the member joins the staff pool unassigned and is assigned by the player via the staff surface.
  - As a player, when I hire a Delivery Driver I want to click it afterwards and assign it to one of my Food/Commerce businesses, so that its adjacency purchase discount actually applies.
  - As a player, when an unassigned business-staff member has no matching business yet, I want to see it labelled as *unassigned business staff* (not management company), with costs and benefits behaving accordingly, so I know I must either build a matching business or lay the member off.
- **Human player (competitive)** — the same flow, restricted to the businesses their seat owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business-staff hire is unchanged and unassigned is first-class. Hiring a business-staff card (`staffCardScope(card) === 'business'`) from the general market row joins the player's staff pool with **no** `employedAtSlot` and **no** hire-time destination step (Q1-B). An unassigned business-staff member receives no business-scope benefits while its salary is still charged (Q2-B); management-company staff hire is unchanged.
- *Assign to business* affordance. From the staff-management surface (the roster overlay opened from the Staff Pile / a member click), an unassigned business-staff member offers an *Assign to business* action; the player picks a destination that satisfies the existing placement predicate (`canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`: business-type match via `staffMatchesBusiness`, free employment slot via `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, competitive ownership via `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). The assignment is executed through `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` — initial placement of an unassigned member stays action-free, a later move of an employed member stays 1 action — and is undoable and logged.
- No legal destination is handled gracefully. When no business the acting seat may employ at matches the member's `allowedBusinessTypes` with a free slot, the member simply remains unassigned (Q2-B): the assign action reports the reason (e.g. "no matching business with a free employment slot") and spends nothing; the member keeps appearing as unassigned business staff until a legal destination exists or it is laid off.
- Roster and type surfaces classify by card type (Q3-A). The management-company roster and Staff Pile list management-company staff only; unassigned business staff are surfaced as an explicit *unassigned business staff* group with the assign affordance and are never presented as management-company staff; employed business staff appear on their business (Manage Card) as today. Effect semantics keyed on `employedAtSlot` are unchanged.
- Lay-off stays available for unassigned business staff. Dismissal of an unassigned business-staff member works from the staff surface with the same quoted cost (one turn's salary + the salary-scaled reputation cost) as other doors.
- Single-player AI / Monte-Carlo hires place business staff (Q3-A). In AI-driven play (Monte Carlo / auto-play), a business-staff hire places the member at a legal destination business as part of the hire; when no legal destination exists the hire action is not taken, so an AI hire is never silently inert. The competitive AI remains staff-free (unchanged).
- Deterministic automated tests cover the matrix: business-staff hire → unassigned for the human player; the assign affordance's legality matrix (type match / no match / no free slot / opponent-owned destination in competitive / no owned business at all); assign is action-free on initial placement and 1 action on relocation; undo/redo and save/load round-trips; roster and Staff-Pile classification (management-company vs unassigned business staff); AI hire-and-place and AI skip-when-no-destination; management-company hire unchanged — seeded and run through the test skill.
- Documentation updated (Q1-B: "update GDD if necessary"). The hire-flow wording in `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4) is updated to the assign-later model (currently they promise "hiring business staff chooses the destination business"); code comments, JSDoc, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries are updated too.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who hires a business-staff card (such as the Delivery Driver) can click the member afterwards and assign it to the business it works at, so the hire actually does what the card promises — until then it is honestly labelled *unassigned business staff* with its costs, rather than masquerading as a management-company employee.

## Constraints

- **One placement predicate.** Destination legality must reuse `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (and therefore `staffMatchesBusiness`, `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). Do not add a second business-type or ownership check.
- **No hire-time placement step.** Per Q1-B the market-row hire flow is unchanged; the fix is the assign affordance and the classification/doc corrections, not a `placing-staff` phase at hire.
- **Effect semantics stay keyed on `employedAtSlot`.** An unassigned business-staff member's business-scope skills remain inert (the existing scope gate); classification changes affect *display surfaces and AI behaviour*, not buff resolution.
- **Action economy unchanged.** Hire is 1 action; assigning an unassigned member (initial placement) is free; relocating an employed member stays 1 action (`isStaffRelocation`); management-company staff are never placed or relocated.
- **Determinism preserved.** AI/enumeration and applicant-resolution changes must not add or reorder `state.rng` draws in a way that changes seeded outcomes (Monte Carlo baselines may shift only as the intended Q3-A consequence, and must stay seeded/deterministic).
- **Single-player untouched where it should be.** The competitive ownership gate stays a no-op without `ownerTaggedGrid`; existing single-player behaviour passes.
- **No new scope.** Staff salaries, the two-type effect model, the applicant flow and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged; extra opportunities (e.g. rebalancing staff salaries) are recorded as linked work items, not folded in here.
- **Backward-compatible saves.** Loads must tolerate older saves that contain unassigned business staff.

## Existing state

- **Hire path never places.** `purchaseStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1061`) deducts coins, removes the row card and pushes `{ ...card }` into `state.staffCards` (`:1085`) with **no** `employedAtSlot`; `hireStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:904`) simply delegates to it. `canPurchaseStaff` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1043`) only checks presence and coins — never business availability (this is now the chosen behaviour for the player, per Q2-B).
- **UI hires immediately.** `onStaffCardClick` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:785`) validates with `canPurchaseStaff` and executes `hireStaffCardCommand` (`:827`) with no destination step — retained as-is under Q1-B.
- **The engine already knows the card is business staff.** `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:996`) gates on `staffCardScope(member) === 'management-company'` (`:1014`), and `staffCardScope` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:147`) falls back to the template marker for an unplaced card — so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *business* staff to the engine, and `placeStaffOnBusiness` can already place it.
- **The roster uses a different test.** `isBusinessStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:248`) is `employedAtSlot !== undefined`, so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *management-company* staff to every roster/tooltip surface: `buildCompanyRoster` (`src/MainStreetRoster.ts:93`), `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:262`) and `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:701`). That is the visible contradiction ("listed as a business staff member" but sitting in the management company).
- **Effects are inert, salary is not.** Business-scope buffs resolve from `business.employedStaff` (`src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`), so an unplaced member contributes nothing, while `applyStaffOngoingCosts` still charges its salary — the behaviour the producer confirmed as intended (Q2-B).
- **No assign door today.** `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) offers only [Confirm lay-off]; business rows appear only in the Manage Card once the member is already employed (`buildBusinessStaffRows`, `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`); `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1091`) rejects an unplaced member (`employedAtSlot == null`) and `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:632`) therefore never offers it. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) is the correct action-free initial-placement command but has **no live UI caller**.
- **Docs promise the superseded model.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` state that hiring business staff "also chooses the destination business — its initial placement is free and part of the hire action"; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope).
- **Single-player AI hires without placing.** `enumerateLegalActions` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:837-860`) offers `hire-staff` for any affordable, not-already-employed staff card, with no placement step, so a Monte-Carlo AI hire of business staff is inert (Q3-A fixes this).
- **Tests.** `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts` asserts that hiring *management-company* staff never assigns a destination; `staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts` covers the coin/hand mechanics only; no test covers the assign-affordance flow or roster classification of unassigned business staff.

## Desired change

1. Keep the market-row hire exactly as it is (Q1-B): business staff join unassigned; no destination step.
2. Add the *Assign to business* interaction for unassigned business-staff members: an affordance on the staff surface (roster overlay / member click), a destination picker derived from `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`, executed via `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (action-free initial placement), undoable and logged.
3. Correct the classification surfaces (Q3-A): `buildCompanyRoster`, `selectManagementCompanyStaff`-driven displays and `buildStaffPileTooltip` must not present business-staff members as management-company staff; an explicit *unassigned business staff* group/row with the assign affordance (and lay-off) is added.
4. Align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path (Q3-A): business-staff hires place the member at a legal destination as part of the hire, or the hire is skipped when none exists.
5. Update the rules/GDD/catalogue docs to the assign-later model (Q1-B "update GDD if necessary").
6. Cover the matrix with deterministic tests; keep saves backward compatible (unassigned members load unchanged and remain assignable — no silent place/delete/reclassify).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — `buildCompanyRoster` (`:93`) classifies by `staffCardScope`; an *unassigned business staff* group with assign affordance data (reuse the `buildMoveStaffAffordance`-style destination derivation, but accepting unplaced members).
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — display classification for unassigned members; `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`:262`) / `isBusinessStaffCard` (`:248`) usage split between display and effects.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`:1906`) gains an *unassigned business staff* section with [ Assign to business ] (and [ Lay off ]); the assign destination picker flow.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`:701`) excludes unassigned business staff; an assign affordance builder (`buildAssignStaffAffordance`) listing legal destinations for an unplaced member.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — assign flow wiring (destination-pick phase or reuse of `moving-staff` with an accept-unplaced predicate); `onMoveStaffClick` (`:362`) / `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1091`) boundary.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`:922`) is the assignment command (may need an unplaced-member legality path; `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` already accepts one).
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `enumerateLegalActions` (`:837`) hire-staff for business staff carries/requires a legal destination slot (hire-and-place composite), skipped when none; `executeAction` handling.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — any legality tweaks to expose the assign action and confirm `placeStaffOnBusiness` handles the unplaced member (it already does via `staffCardScope`).
- `tests/main-street/staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts`, `staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts`, `staff-placement-commands.test.ts`, `company-roster.test.ts`, `staff-pile.test.ts`, `staff-movement.test.ts`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`-based fixtures — new assign-flow, classification, save/load and AI hire-and-place coverage.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — hire-flow wording updated to the assign-later model.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB` — *Implement two-type staff redesign deltas in card data and engine* (introduced the business/management-company split and the `staffCardScope` marker).
- `MS-0MW4MSNMJ006E9JH` — *add skill scope classification and type-consistent assignment* (the scope gate that makes an unassigned business-staff skill inert).
- `MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA` — *Company roster overlay: view and lay off management-company staff* (the roster this member wrongly appears in; the surface gaining the assign affordance).
- `MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM` / `MS-0MWCB35QG0030XU6` — *Roster model* / *Manage Card: staff rows and per-row move* (the row/move patterns to reuse).
- `MS-0MWBB146L005SU31` — *Player hired staff, staff went to AI business* (the sibling ownership bug in the same hire/placement area; established the save-repair precedent and the ownership predicate).
- `MS-0MUOSUKUC004G2VO` / `MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1` — *staff movement* / *gate relocation with 1 action* (`placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` and `isStaffRelocation`).
- `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND` — *Staff effects are not implemented* (open; the inert-effect symptom overlaps but is a separate defect).
- Earlier staff-placement work: `MS-0MU3BTSQ8006ZRCU` (placement engine/commands), `MS-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1` (per-business `allowedBusinessTypes` / `employedStaff`), `CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ` (specialization applicants), `CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX` (walk-on applicant flow).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer confirmed)

- **D1 — Q1 answered (b): post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only.** No hire-time destination picker; the market-row hire flow is unchanged (member joins unassigned). The GDD/core-rules/catalogue wording that currently promises hire-time placement is updated to the assign-later model (in scope, per the producer's "update GDD if necessary"). The producer's phrase "hire goes to the hand" is read as *joins the staff pool / Staff Pile*: staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55) — if the producer intended the card hand instead, that is a much larger scope change and should be raised at planning.
- **D2 — Q2 answered (b): hire proceeds unassigned, benefits not received, costs remain.** When a business-staff hire has no legal destination, the hire is not refused; the member stays unassigned, its business-scope effects are inert, and its salary is still charged. The assign action surfaces the reason and spends nothing.
- **D3 — Q3 answered (a): both.** Roster/Staff-Pile classification is corrected (unassigned business staff shown as *unassigned business staff*, never management-company), and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff at a legal destination or skips the hire (competitive AI stays staff-free).
- **A4 — No silent save repair.** Unlike the competitive cross-seat repair (`MS-0MWBCX7MS00960BH`), an unassigned business-staff member is *not* silently placed on load — the player assigns it (or it stays unassigned until they do).
- **A5 — Scope is classification + assign UI + AI hire placement + docs.** No salary, effect-strength, tier or card-data changes; any such opportunity is a linked follow-up item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix shape): How should a business-staff hire get onto a business?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only (hire unassigned, assign later); update GDD if necessary." Decision recorded as **D1**. Interpretation note: the producer's follow-up "hire goes to the hand" is treated as *the staff pool / Staff Pile*, because staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55; `staff-general-market-state.test.ts`). If the producer intended the card hand, that must be raised at planning as a scope change.
- **Q2 (no legal destination): When a business-staff hire has no matching business with a free slot, what should happen?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — the hire goes through as unassigned; benefits are not received (effects inert until employed) and costs remain (salary charged)." Decision recorded as **D2**.
- **Q3 (scope): Should the fix also correct roster classification and align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(a) — both: roster classification correction and single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire alignment." Decision recorded as **D3**.
- **Q: Which hire path produced the reported Delivery Driver?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the general market row (`onStaffCardClick` → `hireStaffCardCommand` → `hireStaffCard` → `purchaseStaffCard`), which is the only non-applicant hire path and never assigns `employedAtSlot`. The walk-on applicant path does place business staff (`hireStaffApplicant` sets `employedAtSlot = pending.targetSlotIndex`). Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Is the Delivery Driver business staff or management-company staff?** — Answer (agent, evidence): business staff. `src/card-data.csv` ships `handSlotsAdded` and `actionsPerTurn` empty and `allowedBusinessTypes = Food|Commerce`, so `staffCardScope` returns `'business'`; `docs/game/card-catalog.md` classifies its Type as `Business`. The runtime only *downgrades* it to management-company because `employedAtSlot` is absent. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Why does clicking the member offer no assignment?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the Company Roster row (`showCompanyRosterDialog`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) renders only a lay-off button, and the relocation affordance (`buildMoveStaffAffordance` → `canMoveStaffOnBusiness`) rejects a member with `employedAtSlot == null`. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` exists but has no UI caller. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Do the docs currently promise hire-time placement?** — Answer (agent, evidence): yes — `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` both state that hiring business staff chooses the destination business as part of the free initial placement; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope). Source: repo inspection.

# Business expense breakdown ignores the Bookkeeper per-business reduction

## Goal

Make the Turn Summary's Business costs breakdown reconcile to the committed
total when a business employs a Bookkeeper: today the tooltip's per-business
items use the card's raw `ongoingCost` while the engine charges the
Bookkeeper-reduced cost, so the difference is presented as a coin clamp.

Discovered from: `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` (per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats).

## Evidence

- `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) charges
  `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost(state, i, cost)` — the slot's own
  `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` (Bookkeeper, −20%) applied before the
  street-wide Cost Cutter reduction.
- `expenseLineBreakdown` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) builds each
  business item from `(slot as BusinessCard).ongoingCost` with no per-business
  reduction, so `sum(items) + streetReduction` exceeds the committed line when a
  Bookkeeper is employed.
- `buildExpenseLineTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`)
  then reports the residual as "limited to the coins available", which is
  misleading: no clamp occurred.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business expense breakdown items expose the Bookkeeper's per-business reduction as a named modifier (`base + sum(modifiers) === coins`), using `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` and the same helpers the engine charges with.
- The breakdown reconciles exactly to the committed business total for a state with an employed Bookkeeper, with no spurious clamp line in the tooltip.
- Single-player and competitive seats both show the corrected breakdown, with the same detail level on every tab.
- Deterministic tests cover a Bookkeeper-reduced business in both modes, added to the existing tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
- Presentational only: no engine change, no state mutation, no RNG, no new localisable copy beyond the existing `t()` keys.

## Impact

A player who hires a Bookkeeper sees the discount named in the Business costs tooltip instead of a phantom "coins available" clamp.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — `expenseLineBreakdown` business branch
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` (read-only reuse)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — `buildExpenseLineTooltip` reconciliation
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — Bookkeeper breakdown cases

# Apply Bookkeeper reduction in business expense breakdown

## Goal

Fix the `expenseLineBreakdown` function in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` so that the business expense breakdown items reflect the same Bookkeeper per-business reduction that the engine charges with via `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost`.

## Evidence

- **Engine path** (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:495-502`): charges `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost(state, i, cost)` = `roundInt(ongoingCost * (1 - computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct(state, i)))`
- **Breakdown path** (`MainStreetTurnSummary.ts:1349`): uses raw `(slot as BusinessCard).ongoingCost` with no reduction
- **Tooltip** (`MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts:269`): reports the residual as "limited by available coins" — misleading when no clamp occurred

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business expense breakdown items use `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct(state, slotIndex)` to derive per-business `coins`, matching the engine's `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost` logic
- A named modifier (using the Bookkeeper skill name) appears on each business that has a Bookkeeper reduction, with the modifier value = `base - coins`
- The invariant `base + sum(modifiers) === coins` holds for each business item
- No spurious "limited by available coins" clamp line appears in the tooltip when the only discrepancy is the Bookkeeper reduction
- Single-player and competitive seats both show the corrected breakdown with the same detail level
- Presentational only: no engine change, no state mutation, no RNG, no new localisable copy

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — import `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct`; modify business branch in `expenseLineBreakdown`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — no changes needed (tooltip already handles modifiers; clamp line logic corrects automatically)
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` (read-only import)
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — the test suite (child `MS-0MWEQLYCH006NQ4M`) that validates these changes

## Dependencies

- Depends on test child `MS-0MWEQLYCH006NQ4M` being completed first (test-first ordering)

## Impact

A player who employs a Bookkeeper now sees the −20% ongoing-cost discount named on the affected business in the Turn Summary's Business costs tooltip, instead of a misleading "limited by available coins" clamp line.
